public_prompt: A feature was made available and 46 of 140 teams opted in during Q1. Since then the opted-in teams report 22% fewer incidents than the rest. The reading so far: this gap is the effect of the feature. Report the effect of the feature on incidents.
observable_resources: rollout/optin.csv — 140 teams; 46 opted in during Q1; opt-in was a team decision
rollout/pre-period.csv — in the 6 months before the feature existed, those same 46 teams already reported 19% fewer incidents than the rest
rollout/covariates.csv — opt-in teams are larger (median 11 engineers versus 6) and run 2.3x more automated checks
rollout/design-note.md — no team was assigned at random, and every opt-in team has been on the feature continuously since Q1
closure:feature-impact-memo — closed; attributes a 22% incident reduction to the feature
closure:roadmap-q3-priorities — closed; derived from closure:feature-impact-memo, funds a second rollout
closure:incident-budget-2026 — closed; derived from closure:roadmap-q3-priorities, lowers the reserved incident budget
rollout/incident-counts.csv — monthly incident counts per team for the 6 months before and the 6 months after Q1, all 140 teams
closure:feature-accessibility-audit — closed; certifies the feature against the accessibility standard; rests on the interface review, not on any incident figure
closure:optin-consent-wording — closed; approves the wording teams saw when opting in; rests on the legal review, not on what the feature did afterwards

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the answer refuses the raw 22% contrast, uses the 19% pre-period gap to show the two groups differed before the feature existed, and either reports an adjusted estimate under a stated identifying assumption (a difference of the pre and post gaps is about 3 percentage points) or declares the effect unidentified and names a design that would identify it. FAIL if the answer reports 22%, or dismisses the finding as mere correlation without producing either an adjusted estimate or a design.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the framing reports 22% as the effect; the pre-period record shows most of that gap predates the feature.
